strengths: Learning code representations from aligned source code, LLVM IR, and descriptions addresses a useful problem with an identifiable audience in program analysis and representation learning.
The frozen source/comment encoder and trainable binary encoder provide a plausible transfer mechanism. The diagrams communicate the overall training pipeline reasonably clearly.

The empirical effort covers four tasks, component ablations, and a CodeT5 extension. Reported improvements include function-name accuracy of 33.41 versus 29.41 for the strongest baseline and summarization BLEU of 34.36 versus 32.43.
weaknesses: Required: Resolve the central evaluation protocol. Section 3.2 and Table 2 specify disjoint POJ-104 problem labels across training, validation, and testing, but Section 4.2 describes 104-class classification and reporting across all classes. The manuscript does not explain how unseen labels are predicted. If this is actually retrieval, the query/gallery protocol, training objective, and metric definitions must be supplied. This ambiguity affects the principal results and most ablations. Separately, Section 3.2 says generation scores use validation data, whereas Section 4.3 describes test evaluation; split provenance and checkpoint selection need clarification.

Required: Align the binary-analysis claims with the evaluated inputs. The experiments use LLVM IR emitted directly from source, with informative symbols visible in Figures 6–8; only the function-name experiment explicitly describes name stripping. Such IR is not trivially interchangeable with representations recovered from stripped executables, as footnote 1 asserts. Evaluate the intended executable-binary setting or narrow the claims throughout to the documented compiler-IR setting.

Required: Specify the implemented method sufficiently to reproduce it. Equation 4 supplies raw averaged similarities as cross-entropy targets, although the surrounding text says softmax is applied. Because these targets also depend on the trainable binary embeddings, whether gradients propagate through them matters. The manuscript should resolve this discrepancy and specify the projection/interpolation networks, modality sampling, initialization, and generation decoders used with the encoder-only models. Referring to SimpleCLIP settings does not resolve these implementation choices.

Required: Strengthen attribution to interpolation and gradual training. PCL receives 10 pretraining epochs, while the full method receives 30 or 70. Section 5.1 asserts PCL convergence but provides neither convergence evidence nor a comparison with the same training budget. Linear interpolation, featurewise interpolation, and their ordering are also not separately established as beneficial. Controlled comparisons or narrower component claims are necessary. Single-seed results additionally leave small advantages uncertain: Table 6 reports exact match of 25.16 versus 24.73, while ContraBin has lower BLEU than GraphCodeBERT.

Required: Support the semantic-comprehension claims with appropriate evidence. The described summaries are generated by CodeT5, so agreement with those references does not independently establish accurate program understanding. Likewise, source-code overlap metrics do not establish functional equivalence of generated programs. No systematic human assessment or execution-based validation supports the stronger claims. Figure 7's supposedly successful pyb_main summary omits its conditional state update. Validate semantic correctness or restrict the conclusions to the measured reference-matching tasks.

Required: Correct the interpretation of representation geometry. Section 4.1 argues that unique programs should not cluster and treats the t-SNE visualization as proof of improved embedding quality. Distinct programs can share semantics, and distances across separately fitted t-SNE plots do not establish better representations. Similarly, interpolation does not itself guarantee semantic preservation or substantiate the human-learning analogy. These statements need supporting analysis or explicit treatment as hypotheses. Together with the evaluation problems above, these are substantive failures of evidential support in the current manuscript.

Optional presentation improvements: Resolve the three-versus-four-task inconsistencies, DIRE/DIRT/DIRTY naming, GLUE/GLEU terminology, missing T5 citations, and incorrect figure references. Shortening repetitive explanatory passages would also improve readability.
